toegepas.voor: Daarna bars die dop oop aan die een kant van die saad.
toegepas.na: Daarna bars die dop aan die een kant van die saad oop.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The particle of the separable verb 'oopbars' sits more naturally at the end of the clause.
toegepas.fout: The particle 'oop' of the separable verb is split off before the prepositional phrase, which reads as loose spoken order in written text.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Placing 'oop' at the end of the clause is the standard written Afrikaans order and the meaning (the shell splits on one side) is unchanged.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Dan' reads as a next step in time; 'So' makes clear that this set-up means only the light is different.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Dan' already reads naturally as 'in that case' here, and 'So' would repeat the 'So' that opens the block's last sentence ('So word die stam lank en swak').

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Avoids the loose 'n hele klomp' and the repeated 'hele' in the very next sentence ('n hele nuwe plant).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n Hele klomp sade' is natural plain Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader that stresses how many seeds there are, and the following 'n hele nuwe plant' contrasts with it rather than jarring; 'baie' only reads differently.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: maak baie maklik wortels op hierdie manier
laat_vaar_vorige.na: maak op hierdie manier baie maklik wortels
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the adverbial of manner sits more naturally before the object than trailing at the end.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original word order reads naturally; moving the adverbial is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'voor hom gegroei' (grew before it, the seed) reads awkwardly and 'hom' for the seed clashes with 'dit' elsewhere; 'al voorheen' keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'al voorheen' loses the relation 'before it (the seed)' and is vaguer, while the original is correct Afrikaans.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat om te meet en aan te teken
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Tel hoeveel blare die plantjie elke week het.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Tel elke week hoeveel blare die plantjie het.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'elke week' belongs with the instruction 'tel' (count weekly), not inside the counted clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is natural Afrikaans and already means counting the leaves each week; the reorder is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Two attributive adjectives before a noun read more naturally separated by a comma than joined by 'en', especially straight after the list 'lank, dun en swak'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'klein en bleek blaartjies' is natural Afrikaans, so the comma form is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Watter saad dink jy ontkiem eerste?
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Watter saad, dink jy, ontkiem eerste?
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'dink jy' is an inserted clause here and is set off by commas, which also keeps the reader from reading 'saad dink' together.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Watter saad dink jy ontkiem eerste?' is the normal Afrikaans question with 'dink jy' as the main clause, not an inserted one, so the commas are optional and add nothing.
